vm.testHarness: Interactive Task Scheduler launches Node, which starts Argus through Explorer Shell.Application.
vm.environmentNote: VM without GPU acceleration: orb about 30 FPS and expanded background about 15 FPS at the 60 FPS setting. The background check ran with a focused window and only shows that the rate stays above the old 10 FPS limit; the inactive-window rate was measured in the isolated host test.
invalidatedAttempts: First run stopped because the version rename also changed the fixed backup file name expected by the test tool; tool corrected, product unchanged, run repeated.
Guest control channel stopped responding twice around the restart step; only the VM was reset, polling slowed, and the restart and logoff steps repeated with success.

rendererTests.menus: unstable on the host: failed 3 times on this source and once on 0.58.31 while the desktop was in use, then passed 5 of 5 on both; focus dependence is the likely cause, not proven

frameMeasurement.setting: 60 FPS idle and moving, Fluid, inactive window, one minute without input, 144.9 Hz animation clock, isolated 1280x900 test window, two runs each

knownPreexistingTests.result: not run: it starts the real main process, which is not done on the host next to the installed Argus. The installed main process was exercised in the VM instead.

limitations: A Windows session end in which Argus receives no message is still reported as an unclean end.
Forced power loss cannot be distinguished from forced process termination.
In a focused window the 10 FPS limit after one idle minute still applies at the saving rates.
The real display output on the 60 Hz monitor was not measured; the measurements cover the frame schedule inside Argus.
Choosing 60 FPS costs measurably more CPU and GPU than the previous 48/10 FPS.
Voice activation in a hidden window was not tested with a microphone.
The optional Apple mode is not part of this source state, so only the classic mode was tested.
